rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.7, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.5, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=iter-1 ONBOARDING/FEASIBILITY fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained on re-split Breast-CT (train 3600 / val 200 / test 200, seed 20260703), val=200. wdm_recon = few-step Haar-wavelet flow-matching prior + DPS guidance + hard CG DC-step. Prior ckpt = MAYO-TRAINED fast_diffusion_wavelet_unconstrained.pt (fd_out_scale=0.05, n_train=2000, val_flow_loss=0.020) -- NO breast-native wavelet prior exists, so this is the documented Mayo-prior fallback; breast mu ranges to 0.5 (10x Mayo's ~0.05 normaliser) so a domain-normalisation mismatch is EXPECTED. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: none for this slug; nearest = Mayo wdm-wavelet-uncon run (search-20260620-01) whose best knobs were NFE8/init_t0.4/eta1.0/dc_relax1.0, all hr=0 (regime-bound below the dense-Mayo FBP floor). Breast is the OPPOSITE regime: 128-view SPARSE, where the design doc predicts the wavelet prior + DC-step help MOST (data under-constrains, prior fills the null space). (2) Failure mode: N/A onboarding; goal = does the recon run on breast val=200 under the HARD 20-min budget and where does it sit vs the 128-view sparse FBP baseline? (3) ONE KNOB: N/A baseline -- mirrors the Mayo sibling iter-1 recon knobs (8-step, FBP init t=0.7, eta1.0, DC on, CG5, relax0.5). (4) HYPOTHESIS: the Mayo-trained wavelet prior on 512^2 breast reconstructs at ~8 NFE inside 20 min; because of the 10x out_scale mismatch the prior term is largely mis-scaled, so the DC-step (CG onto the measured sparse sinogram) will dominate and hr likely lands modest/near-baseline -- quantifying that gap IS the finding. (5) BUDGET: mayo 512^2 wdm 8-step over 214 val took ~416s; breast 200 val at 512^2 comparable -> well inside 20 min (30-min sbatch wall). (6) Loop continues; iter-2 dispatched on landing. Reserved levers iters 2-5: fd_recon_dc_relax, fd_recon_init_t, fd_recon_steps, fd_recon_eta.
